lines.trans: I thought surely not, yet it really is you, Cindy? Why are you standing out here in the rain—whom are you waiting for?
Producer Baek Seung-chan—there is something I need to tell him.
Come inside—I will call Seung-chan and tell him to come to my place. You will catch a cold out here.
Rather than coffee, a hot cup of tea should warm you up—wait right here, I will brew some.

words.gloss: I will boil it for you

lines.trans: Does your agency know you are here? Did something happen with CEO Byun after you went back?
Even in your eyes, Producer, do I look as if I am faking even my sincere feelings?
Someone told me it seems I act out even my sincerity—honestly I do not know anymore, maybe I really do.
You can easily picture what you will be doing ten years from now, right, Producer? I cannot.
I cannot picture myself in ten years—forget ten years, I do not even know five years or one year ahead.
The harder I thrash around to escape, the deeper into a swamp I feel myself sinking.

Even in your eyes, Producer, do I look as if I am faking even my sincere feelings?
Someone told me it seems I act out even my sincerity—honestly I do not know anymore, maybe I really do.

See you next time!

meanings.note: Used as noun (감기).

examples.text: 들어가자, 내가 승찬이한테 전화해서 우리 집으로 오라고 그럴게. 이러다 감기 걸려.
examples.trans: Come inside—I will call Seung-chan and tell him to come to my place. You will catch a cold out here.
This point about a cold is really important.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Used as casual past (걸렸어.).

examples.text: 이제 다 됐어, 낙서 지우는 데 좀 시간이 걸렸어. 주차장 도착하면 다시 전화할게.
examples.trans: It is all finished now—scrubbing off the graffiti took a while. I will call again once I reach the parking lot.
Let us do that (it took) right away.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.
I want to wait right now.
How about trying to wait together tomorrow?

meanings.note: commonly paired with 좋다 ('good') or 나쁘다 ('bad')

examples.trans: The weather is clear, so I'm in a good mood.

examples.text: 칭찬을 들으니 기분이 날아갈 것 같아요.
examples.trans: Hearing the compliment makes me feel on cloud nine.

끓여주다.gloss: I will boil it for you

meanings.en: I will boil it for you
meanings.note: Used as promissive -ㄹ게 (끓여줄게.).

examples.text: 커피 말고 차를 따뜻하게 해서 마시면 좋을 것 같은데 잠깐만 기다려, 따뜻하게 끓여줄게.
examples.trans: Rather than coffee, a hot cup of tea should warm you up—wait right here, I will brew some.
Let us do that (I will boil it for you) right away.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

examples.text: 나 십 년 동안 시키는 대로 다 했잖아요.
examples.trans: For ten years, I did everything you told me to do.

examples.text: 이십 년 넘게 친구 설정으로 지냈는데 쉽진 않겠지.
examples.trans: You lived as friends for over twenty years, so changing that won't be easy.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: Used as noun + directional (늪으로).

examples.text: 발버둥 치면 칠수록 늪으로 빠져드는 기분이에요.
examples.trans: The harder I thrash around to escape, the deeper into a swamp I feel myself sinking.
This point about into a swamp is really important.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used as adverbial -게 (따뜻하게).

examples.text: 커피 말고 차를 따뜻하게 해서 마시면 좋을 것 같은데 잠깐만 기다려, 따뜻하게 끓여줄게.
examples.trans: Rather than coffee, a hot cup of tea should warm you up—wait right here, I will brew some.
It is really warmly compared to what I expected.
I want to drink right now.
How about trying to drink together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match
meanings.note: E.g., 사이즈가 맞다 ('the size fits').

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

examples.text: 있는 그대로, 내 모습 그대로? 알겠어요.
examples.trans: Just as I am, my true self? Got it.
The topic of appearance, true self came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 얘 지금 살려고 발버둥 치는 거 안 보여? 이런 거 보면 인간이 진짜 제일 잔인해.
examples.trans: Do you not see it struggling to stay alive right now? Seeing things like this, humans really are the cruelest.
Here the word for 'frantic struggle' is key.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
I want to is it visible? right now.
How about trying to is it visible? together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used with 오다 or 내리다.

examples.trans: It is raining.
The rain stopped.

meanings.note: Used as present adnominal (빠져드는).

examples.text: 발버둥 치면 칠수록 늪으로 빠져드는 기분이에요.
examples.trans: The harder I thrash around to escape, the deeper into a swamp I feel myself sinking.
Let us do that (sinking deeper) right away.

examples.text: 선? 검사? 설마 검사가 예쁘기까지 하겠어?
examples.trans: A blind date? A prosecutor? Could a prosecutor really be pretty too?

examples.text: 설마 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (surely not, could it be), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

examples.text: 신디 씨가 오늘 뭐 연기하신 거 있어요?
examples.trans: Did Cindy put on any acting today?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 연기하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (acted, put on an act (honorific)).

examples.text: 예상을 전혀 못 한 것 같고 작전으로는 성공인데 희한하네.
examples.trans: She didn't expect it at all, so the operation succeeded, yet something feels odd.
The topic of expectation came up during this shoot.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this
meanings.note: Contracted from 이러하다.

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.
Test
Test2

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.en: for a moment; briefly; a second
meanings.note: Used to soften requests or indicate a very short duration.

examples.trans: Do you have a moment?
Just a second, I'll be right there.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: The person called is marked with 에게 or 한테 (e.g., 친구한테 전화하다).

examples.trans: Please call me when you arrive.
I'll call right now.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: Used colloquially as an adverb meaning 'truly'.
Also used as a noun.

examples.trans: It's seriously cold today.
I thank you sincerely.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: Short for 자동차.

examples.trans: This is my father's car.
I parked the car in the parking lot.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to cause (trouble)
meanings.note: Used in idioms like 사고를 치다 (to cause trouble).

examples.trans: I caused trouble.
I caused trouble. (2)

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 커피 시킬 때 보면 돼요, 이름 긴 거 시키는 사람들 있거든.
examples.trans: Just watch when they order coffee—some people order drinks with super long names.
Here the word for 'coffee' is key.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
My office is close to home.
I go to work at the office at 9 a.m.

meanings.note: Used as noun + time -에 (후에).

examples.text: 피디님은 10년 후에 내가 뭐 하고 있을지 이런 거 다 예상이 되시죠? 나는 안 돼요.
examples.trans: You can easily picture what you will be doing ten years from now, right, Producer? I cannot.

examples.text: 10년 후의 내 모습 난 모르겠어요. 10년 후 아니라 5년 후, 1년 후도 모르겠어요.
examples.trans: I cannot picture myself in ten years—forget ten years, I do not even know five years or one year ahead.
